authority to enact legislation aimed at eradicating slavery and involuntary servitude,
which has been interpreted to extend to addressing the vestiges of racial discrimination.
This constitutional foundation supports Congress's recent statute prohibiting racial
discrimination in real estate transactions, as such discrimination perpetuates economic
inequality and social disenfranchisement akin to the effects of slavery. By framing racial
discrimination in housing as a form of involuntary servitude, Congress can utilize its
enforcement powers to promote equality and protect civil rights, reinforcing the
Thirteenth Amendment's commitment to dismantling systemic oppression. Thus, the statute
serves as a modern application of Congressional authority to combat racial discrimination,
guided by the historical context of the amendment.

Compensatory damages play a crucial role in contract law as they serve to financially
restore the nonbreaching party to the position they would have occupied had the contract
been fully performed. These damages are intended to cover the actual loss suffered due to
the breach, including lost profits and any consequential damages that arise directly from
the nonperformance of the contract. By focusing on the principle of restitution,
compensatory damages ensure that the nonbreaching party is not unjustly enriched or left
in a worse position as a result of the breach. This legal remedy underscores the
importance of contractual obligations and seeks to uphold the integrity of agreements by
providing a tangible means of redress for those affected. Thus, compensatory damages
reflect a fundamental aspect of contract enforcement, aiming to balance the interests of
both parties involved.
answers.explanation: correct because it accurately describes how compensatory damages aim to financially restore the nonbreaching party to their pre-breach position by covering actual losses and ensuring they do not suffer from the breach of contract.
